claims.text: A surface modification treatment can produce a protective surface layer on stainless steel.
Monitoring and optimizing the treatment with in-situ localized electrochemical impedance spectroscopy will significantly enhance corrosion resistance in extreme corrosive environments.
Standard stainless steel has reduced endurance in extreme corrosive conditions.
The reduced endurance of stainless steel is caused by limitations in its intrinsic passive film.
The proposed treatment modifies the surface at the micro- or nanoscale.
LEIS can monitor the surface modification in real time and in situ.
The treatment forms a tailored, robust, and homogeneous passive surface layer.
The passive surface layer impedes the ingress of corrosive species.
Surface modification improves the characteristics of the stainless-steel passive film.
LEIS measures impedance changes that correlate with passive-film integrity.
Real-time LEIS monitoring enables optimization of the surface modification.
The optimized modified layer prevents corrosion more effectively than the untreated surface.
Modified stainless steel will exhibit higher impedance than untreated stainless steel under identical extreme corrosive conditions.
Modified stainless steel will have a lower corrosion rate than untreated stainless steel under identical extreme corrosive conditions.
Modified stainless steel will retain better surface integrity than untreated stainless steel under identical extreme corrosive conditions.
The expected improvement is specific to extremely corrosive conditions and may not transfer directly to less aggressive environments.
The surface treatment does not alter the bulk properties of the steel.
